title: Split athena-core --lib into parts across test shards
summary: Retry of job 20261102-154551-5qcd (dispatched, never verified, no findings): teach `xtask test-shard` to split one test binary into parts by test-name module prefix, split athena-core's `--lib` into several parts that the six shards share, with a coverage test, shard timings and a CHANGELOG entry. Audience: CI maintainers and the verifier judging shard balance and exactly-once coverage.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust in xtask.
Unit and integration tests cover the new filtered units.
Criteria check balance and exactly-once coverage, not wiring.
Behavior criteria name cargo run/test commands.
Timings file and CHANGELOG state their basis.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Previous result, job 20261102-154551-5qcd: it was never verified and recorded no findings, so there is nothing to fix. Its six changed files are kept as deliverables (re-done from base): CHANGELOG.md, xtask/shard-timings.txt, xtask/src/main.rs, xtask/src/shard.rs, xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs, and the new xtask/tests/shard_parts.rs. Its out_of_scope items stand.

Code Survey: the existing sharding code is in xtask/src/shard.rs and xtask/src/main.rs (test-shard entry point, Unit selector, timings parse and balancer) with xtask/shard-timings.txt as data; athena-core unit tests live under crates/athena-core/src. No record files are added under crates/, so no records allow-list or AnyRecord round-trip applies. Coverage is measured directly by listing names with `cargo test -p athena-core --lib -- --list` and matching each against part filters.

Code survey: crates/athena-core/src (module names such as gh, reading, run, run_pin_tests, hestia, status, steward) gives the prefixes; the skip-based catch-all part guarantees new modules run exactly once.

xtask/shard-timings.txt currently lists `athena-core --lib 15.00`; the replacement part lines use estimates summing to about 255s derived from run 41469096430, labeled as estimates. No GitHub access is needed.
Governance: ci.yml and the shard count are unchanged; the CI workflow needs no change because shards call `xtask test-shard`.
Existing code is not needed beyond xtask/src/shard.rs; nothing new is designed.

acceptance_criteria.text: xtask/src/shard.rs lets a unit carry a test-name filter (module prefixes plus a skip-based catch-all), prints it in the --dry-run line and runs it as `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --lib -- <filter>`; Grep of xtask/shard-timings.txt shows athena-core --lib as at least two part lines, not one.
Run `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard K 6 --dry-run` for K=0..5: athena-core --lib parts appear in at least two different shards, no part appears twice, and no other target is lost or duplicated.

Run `cargo test -p xtask --test shard_parts` (and `--test ci_shards`): a test checks every name from `cargo test -p athena-core --lib -- --list` matches exactly one part's filter, and a negative test shows a dropped or duplicated prefix is rejected.

xtask/shard-timings.txt lists the athena-core parts with estimated seconds summing to about 255s, notes they are estimates from run 41469096430, and no shard's estimated total exceeds roughly the mean plus the largest remaining single unit (lifecycle, 143.22s).

CHANGELOG.md has an entry stating the before numbers: athena-core --lib one binary of 821 tests at 255.11s (97% of shard 0's test time), shard 0 test step 5m45s vs shard 4 1m45s, and the next slowest binaries lifecycle 143.22s, drain 79.32s, retry 49.45s, job_plan 46.35s.

Unit tests in xtask/src/shard.rs for filtered units (assignment keeps every part exactly once, deterministic part ordering, timings round-trip with a filtered selector) pass under `cargo test -p xtask`.

out_of_scope: Changing the number of shards or .github/workflows/ci.yml
Speeding up or editing the athena-core tests themselves
Fetching anything from GitHub or re-measuring timings
Splitting other binaries such as lifecycle.rs
